_about: The sandbox's classes (classes.ts): ships, aircraft and corps that history never built, and the player's own designs. Everything here is behind one switch, g.flags.sandbox, in the grand campaign only: off, the game is exactly as it was. Each row is a variant of a kind the arsenal already orders, named in 'of': ships 'bb' 'cv' 'ca' 'dd' 'ss', aircraft 'ftr' 'bmr', land the corps kinds ('arm', 'mot', ...) and 'para' for an airborne corps. It counts as that kind everywhere a kind is counted, and every field it does not state is its kind's own: 'cost' 'months' 'count' 'yard' from arsenal.json, 'cost' 'months' 'divs' from production.json or arsenal.json 'land' (or tech.json 'units' for 'para'). 'whatif' marks a class of the research tree: the technology that opens it lists 'class:<id>' in its 'unlock'. 'model' is its battle model in battle-models ('land/', 'air/', 'sea/'); 'glider' the glider that carries an airborne class. 'steel' is its own share of the steel bill (arsenal.json 'steel'). 'word' goes into a corps' name: XV Flame Tank Corps. Land fields: 'edges' is a list of what it is worth in battle, each an 'attack' and/or 'defence' multiplier under a 'when' read as for a national ability (traits.json): 'kinds', 'terrain', 'winter', 'works', 'landing' and the rest; 'most' is how many the nation can keep at once in the field and on order; 'oil' multiplies what its kind burns. Aircraft fields: 'fight' multiplies what each aircraft is worth in a fight in the air; 'reach' multiplies how far its fighters and bombers reach; 'night' is the share of its fighters that find a raid by night (in place of the nation's own figure when larger); 'close' multiplies what its fighters are worth on call over a land battle; 'escort' is what each of its bombers counts as escort, as a share of a fighter; 'bomb' multiplies the weight of bombs its bombers put on the land (factories, towns, troops, fieldworks), and 'sea' what they put on ships and shipping; 'oil' multiplies what its aircraft burn. Costs are in production points (shown times a hundred). Figures are a first pass, to be tuned against par after release 1.

classes.label: Breakthrough tank corps
classes.blurb: Seventy-ton tanks with two turrets: a short, heavy gun that blows bunkers apart and a long one for other tanks. Made to break a fortified line, and dear to build and to fuel.

classes.label: Flame tank corps
classes.blurb: Medium tanks that carry a flame projector in place of a gun, with armoured fuel tanks on the rear deck. Terrible in streets, woods and trenches; the fuel they carry makes them a target.

classes.label: Amphibious tank corps
classes.blurb: Tanks with watertight boat hulls and propellers that swim ashore with the first wave. Armour thinned to keep them afloat.

classes.label: Snow tank corps
classes.blurb: Tanks on tracks twice the usual width, with engine heaters and sealed hatches, built for deep snow and bog. Where other tanks stick fast, they keep moving.

classes.label: Tank hunter corps
classes.blurb: Eight-wheeled armoured cars carrying a long tank gun, fast on roads and quick to a threatened sector. Lightly armoured: they ambush tanks rather than duel them.

classes.label: Glider tank corps
classes.blurb: Airborne troops with two-man light tanks, landed in heavy gliders whose noses swing open for the tanks to drive out. They hit harder where they land and hold on longer.

classes.label: Escort fighter wing
classes.blurb: Twin-boom, push-pull fighters with drop tanks, built to fly all the way to the target and back with the bombers. A little heavy in a turning fight.

classes.label: Night fighter wing
classes.blurb: Three-seat twin-engined fighters with radar in the nose and upward-firing cannon. By night they find the bombers that other fighters never see; by day they are slow.

classes.label: Tank-buster wing
classes.blurb: Armoured twin-engined attack aircraft with a long anti-tank gun under the nose, flown on call over the battle. Easy prey for enemy fighters.

classes.label: Gunship wing
classes.blurb: Four-engined bombers that carry guns instead of bombs: eight turrets and a magazine where the bomb bay was. They fly in the formation and shield the bombers around them.

classes.label: Sea hunter wing
classes.blurb: Four-engined flying boats with search radar, torpedoes and depth charges, flown far out over the sea lanes. Little use over land.
